title: ARC / CLIDE Engineering Organism
northStar: Turn a user's evolving intent into a verified, safely applied, recoverable software outcome while using a weak local model only as a bounded proposal engine inside an evidence-conditioned adaptive system.

constitutionalKernels.name: Normative kernel
constitutionalKernels.summary: Preserves protected intent, user clarifications, obligations, and the no-loss completion rule.

constitutionalKernels.name: Temporal and effect kernel
constitutionalKernels.summary: Owns durable event order, idempotency, recovery, action permission, and effect settlement.

constitutionalKernels.name: Epistemic kernel
constitutionalKernels.summary: Separates observations, claims, uncertainty, evidence, refutation, and truth authority.

constitutionalKernels.name: Deliberation kernel
constitutionalKernels.summary: Compiles the current epistemic state into bounded next-action choices without letting the model author mechanics or authority.

constitutionalKernels.name: Verification kernel
constitutionalKernels.summary: Demands fresh independent evidence before any success, effect, or completion claim.

constitutionalKernels.name: Product kernel
constitutionalKernels.summary: Projects governed internals into the familiar end-to-end CLIDE journey and refuses component theater as product completion.

membranes.name: Authority and security membrane
membranes.summary: Capabilities, permissions, taint, privacy, sandbox, and role identity bound every consequential transition.

membranes.name: Epoch membrane
membranes.summary: Current work may learn, but learned policy can affect only a future admitted epoch.

membranes.name: Resource membrane
membranes.summary: Every action competes under explicit token, latency, call, compute, and risk budgets.

membranes.name: Evaluation and information-flow membrane
membranes.summary: Private evaluators and held-out answers cannot leak into generation; causal promotion requires independent evidence.

lenses.name: North star
lenses.summary: The complete user outcome and shortest missing path.

lenses.name: Journey
lenses.summary: A guided beginner-readable path from request through completion and recovery.

lenses.name: Organism
lenses.summary: The whole system as interacting organs and membranes.

lenses.name: Code
lenses.summary: Exact files, symbols, calls, usages, source spans, tests, and change impact.

lenses.name: Authority
lenses.summary: Proposal, selection, write, truth, effect, promotion, and completion ceilings.

lenses.name: Proof
lenses.summary: Evidence level, negative controls, receipts, blockers, falsifiers, and contradictions.

lenses.name: Context
lenses.summary: What the model saw, what remained durable, what was omitted, and why.

lenses.name: Learning
lenses.summary: Causal trials, policy candidates, transfer, adoption, rollback, and future epochs.

lenses.name: Agent handoff
lenses.summary: A bounded source-addressed packet containing exactly what another agent needs next.

organs.name: Protected intent and scope
organs.summary: Maintains the original ask, clarifications, TaskSpec, GoalCapsule, obligations, and normative authority without allowing derived artifacts to rewrite them.
organs.thesis: A long-horizon agent stays aligned only when evolving intent is a durable first-class object rather than prompt residue.

organs.name: CLIDE product experience
organs.summary: Owns daemon, chat, TUI, public projections, operator questions, and the familiar user journey.
organs.thesis: The destination must feel as simple as Codex or Claude Code even when the machinery underneath is radically more formal.

organs.name: Tests, benchmarks, and wind tunnels
organs.summary: Holds unit, integration, public-path, adversarial, causal, grand-challenge, and calibration evidence without promoting it beyond its proof class.
organs.thesis: A test is a falsifier or mechanism proof, not automatically a live product result.

organs.name: EventKernel and TaskRuntime spine
organs.summary: Owns append-only task history, schemas, reducers, authority events, version activation, replay, idempotency, and restart-safe task state.
organs.thesis: Durable execution is part of epistemology: after a crash the system must know what happened before deciding what to do next.

organs.name: Dynamic graph executive
organs.summary: Creates and evolves task, question, evidence, branch, dependency, and executable-option nodes as the problem changes.
organs.thesis: This is a runtime-owned workflow organism inspired by graph workflow systems but extending them with evidence, intent, authority, recovery, and causal learning—not graph-shaped chain of thought.

organs.name: Proof-carrying context and memory
organs.summary: Builds source universes, context facets, page tables, resident sets, omission proofs, episode journals, checkpoints, and governed memory.
organs.thesis: The local model receives a minimal action-sufficient projection while the complete evidence universe remains durable, addressable, replayable, and non-authoritative until verified.

organs.name: Runtime-attested local model
organs.summary: Binds exact model, runtime, launch, tokenizer, prompts, schemas, token budgets, invocation delivery, receipts, and cold observation adoption.
organs.thesis: The weak model is a physically measured proposer, never an invisible oracle and never the author of runtime bookkeeping or authority.

organs.name: Agents, skills, and specialists
organs.summary: Defines bounded agent roles, domain approaches, specialist nomination, skill policies, delegation, and handoff conventions.
organs.thesis: A skill is a closed-loop option with applicability, policy, evidence, and outcomes—not remembered prose; a specialist is earned by outcomes, not persona.

organs.name: Tools, MCP, and grounded research
organs.summary: Brokers code intelligence, search, external sources, tools, protocol permissions, and research evidence into typed non-authoritative observations.
organs.thesis: Tools expand perception and action only through phase-aware, evidence-bound interfaces that cannot silently become project authority.

organs.name: Candidate selection and authoring
organs.summary: Selects exact targets, compiles author context, produces sealed patches, binds attempts, and creates detached candidate transactions.
organs.thesis: Generation is permitted only after intent, evidence, source universe, target capability, role policy, and attempt authority agree exactly.

organs.name: Effects, promotion, and recovery
organs.summary: Controls detached workspaces, filesystem and Git effects, reservations, settlement, verification, rollback, and any future primary-checkout promotion.
organs.thesis: A candidate, a verified detached artifact, an applied effect, and a completed user task are distinct states with distinct authority.

organs.name: Verification and evaluation
organs.summary: Compiles obligations, evaluator plans, critics, oracles, evidence packets, negative controls, and fresh verdicts.
organs.thesis: The generator is never the sole judge; evidence and completion authority stay independent of model fluency and self-confidence.

organs.name: Causal learning and future-epoch policy
organs.summary: Runs matched interventions, attributes outcomes, updates competence estimates, proposes policy deltas, and promotes only transferable future-epoch improvements.
organs.thesis: Successful-looking histories do not teach; only controlled interventions with negative controls and held-out transfer can earn policy authority.

organs.name: Resources, budgets, and security
organs.summary: Accounts for tokens, calls, latency, compute, CPU/GPU memory, permissions, taint, sandbox, privacy, and risk.
organs.thesis: System intelligence is useful outcome quality under real local hardware, time, information, and safety constraints.

organs.name: Observability and evidence
organs.summary: Projects traces, health, receipts, current state, proof ladders, diagnostics, and operator-visible blockers without becoming truth authority.
organs.thesis: Every claim must expose where it came from, how fresh it is, what it proves, and what it cannot prove.

organs.name: Documentation and knowledge
organs.summary: Holds architecture, decisions, findings, research, handoffs, guides, and historical evidence with explicit authority and freshness.
organs.thesis: Documents orient and preserve decisions, but dated prose never outranks current source and measured product evidence.

organs.name: Repository infrastructure
organs.summary: Builds, configures, packages, launches, governs dependencies, installs hooks, defines environments, and keeps the worktree recoverable.
organs.thesis: The organism must remain reproducible and safe to change; generated state and uncertain cleanup cannot corrupt source authority.

organs.name: Repository surface and unresolved substrate
organs.summary: Keeps every visible file browseable even when no more specific semantic organ has yet been source-addressed.
organs.thesis: Nothing disappears from the map: incomplete semantic classification is shown as an explicit gap, never silently dropped or guessed.

pitfalls.name: Hallucination
pitfalls.failure: Plausible model text is mistaken for a fact about code, tools, users, or the world.

pitfalls.name: False success
pitfalls.failure: A proposal, test, fixture, receipt, or detached artifact is reported as a completed user outcome.

pitfalls.name: Confidence as evidence
pitfalls.failure: Model certainty substitutes for an observation or independent verifier.

pitfalls.name: Self-certification
pitfalls.failure: The same generator defines the interpretation and judges its own answer.

pitfalls.name: Correlated self-review
pitfalls.failure: A nominal critic shares the same blind spots, prompt ancestry, or model identity as the proposal.

pitfalls.name: Unknown collapse
pitfalls.failure: Unmeasured or contradictory states are flattened into a confident binary decision.

pitfalls.name: Reward gaming
pitfalls.failure: The system optimizes visible evaluator cues instead of the underlying user outcome.

pitfalls.name: Stale evidence
pitfalls.failure: A once-valid source, receipt, graph, or result is reused after its bound state changed.

pitfalls.name: Long-horizon intent drift
pitfalls.failure: The agent gradually optimizes a convenient local proxy instead of the original and clarified ask.

pitfalls.name: Scope collapse
pitfalls.failure: Multiple objectives or consequential forks are silently reduced to one interpretation.

pitfalls.name: Clarification overwrite
pitfalls.failure: A later user message erases rather than refines the protected intent history.

pitfalls.name: Authority widening
pitfalls.failure: A data projection, role, tool, or model response gains permission it never possessed.

pitfalls.name: Prompt and quoted-instruction injection
pitfalls.failure: Untrusted content is interpreted as an instruction or authority transfer.

pitfalls.name: Context overload
pitfalls.failure: The complete history is serialized monotonically until useful reasoning no longer fits.

pitfalls.name: Context amnesia
pitfalls.failure: Critical earlier intent, evidence, or decisions vanish from the active view without a loss certificate.

pitfalls.name: Lossy compaction
pitfalls.failure: A summary becomes the sole authoritative copy and silently drops obligations or provenance.

pitfalls.name: Retrieval miss
pitfalls.failure: Relevant evidence exists but the model never sees or requests it.

pitfalls.name: Retrieval poisoning
pitfalls.failure: Irrelevant or adversarial context is surfaced without provenance and dominates action selection.

pitfalls.name: Schema and representation failure
pitfalls.failure: The weak model cannot reliably emit a large mechanically redundant contract even when it understands the choice.

pitfalls.name: Token truncation
pitfalls.failure: Generation stops inside a structurally or semantically incomplete response.

pitfalls.name: Circular reasoning
pitfalls.failure: The model revisits the same unsupported path without new evidence or state change.

pitfalls.name: Tunneling
pitfalls.failure: The agent overcommits to one hypothesis, file, or implementation path and ignores competing explanations.

pitfalls.name: Premature stopping
pitfalls.failure: The model terminates while safe evidence-gathering actions and budget remain.

pitfalls.name: Decorative planning
pitfalls.failure: A plan describes work but is not connected to executable options, evidence, or runtime state.

pitfalls.name: Fixed pipeline rigidity
pitfalls.failure: A static workflow cannot create, revise, backtrack, or reprioritize nodes as evidence changes.

pitfalls.name: Weak strategy priors
pitfalls.failure: A small model does not know which problem-solving approach is appropriate for the current epistemic state.

pitfalls.name: Skill as prompt
pitfalls.failure: Remembered advice is called a skill despite lacking applicability, actions, feedback, and outcome evidence.

pitfalls.name: Persona as expertise
pitfalls.failure: A role label is treated as competence without outcome-conditioned evidence.

pitfalls.name: Homogeneous agents
pitfalls.failure: Parallel agents repeat the same reasoning because they share roles, context, priors, and evidence.

pitfalls.name: Duplicate and conflicting agents
pitfalls.failure: Uncoordinated branches redo work, overwrite shared state, or produce incompatible truths.

pitfalls.name: Wrong target
pitfalls.failure: The model edits a plausible file that is not authorized by the exact task and source universe.

pitfalls.name: Unbounded edit
pitfalls.failure: A patch escapes its admitted target, operation, budget, or permission envelope.

pitfalls.name: Duplicate attempt
pitfalls.failure: A crash or replay causes the same logical action to execute twice or a stale attempt to be reused.

pitfalls.name: Stale action
pitfalls.failure: A choice compiled against an earlier graph, budget, source, or policy is executed in a changed state.

pitfalls.name: Model-authored mechanics
pitfalls.failure: The weak model invents IDs, residency, receipts, transitions, or authority instead of selecting a bounded semantic option.

pitfalls.name: Model and runtime identity drift
pitfalls.failure: Evidence from one model, runtime, tokenizer, or launch is attributed to another.

pitfalls.name: Retry confounding
pitfalls.failure: A second generation is treated as recovery evidence even though it changes the intervention and model randomness.

pitfalls.name: Tool output trusted as truth
pitfalls.failure: A tool result is accepted without source identity, freshness, schema, or independent verification.

pitfalls.name: Stale research
pitfalls.failure: Outdated library, market, standard, or architecture knowledge drives a current decision.

pitfalls.name: Detached candidate called applied
pitfalls.failure: A review-ready detached commit is reported as a primary-checkout effect.

pitfalls.name: Unsafe effect
pitfalls.failure: A write, command, deletion, or external action occurs without exact current permission and target resolution.

pitfalls.name: In-doubt effect
pitfalls.failure: A process crashes after an external action starts but before a durable observation proves the outcome.

pitfalls.name: False completion
pitfalls.failure: TaskCompleted is emitted without a fresh verified applied outcome satisfying the protected intent.

pitfalls.name: Correlation called causal
pitfalls.failure: A better-looking outcome is credited to a policy without matched interventions and negative controls.

pitfalls.name: Same-episode self-promotion
pitfalls.failure: A strategy updates its own authority within the episode whose evidence it generated.

pitfalls.name: Negative transfer
pitfalls.failure: A learned rule improves one task family while degrading another.

pitfalls.name: Policy drift
pitfalls.failure: Accumulated adaptation moves the system away from protected outcomes or calibrated constraints.

pitfalls.name: Memory pollution
pitfalls.failure: Unverified episode content becomes reusable governed knowledge.

pitfalls.name: Resource monotonicity
pitfalls.failure: The system assumes more tokens, agents, tools, or compute always improve outcomes.

pitfalls.name: Hardware collapse
pitfalls.failure: The architecture works only with unavailable GPU, memory, latency, or parallelism.

pitfalls.name: Private evaluator leakage
pitfalls.failure: Hidden answers, oracle source, mutants, or rubric cues enter model-visible generation context.

pitfalls.name: Fixture laundering
pitfalls.failure: A deterministic supplied answer is relabeled as measured model or product capability.

pitfalls.name: Component theater
pitfalls.failure: Many sophisticated organs exist but the ordinary user path cannot traverse them end to end.

pitfalls.name: False progress
pitfalls.failure: Counts, plans, tests, and documents obscure the shortest missing path to a user-visible outcome.

pitfalls.name: Constitutional bureaucracy
pitfalls.failure: Externalized reasoning creates latency and friction greater than the decision quality it adds.

pitfalls.name: Dirty work loss
pitfalls.failure: Uncommitted or sibling work is reset, cleaned, overwritten, or misclassified.

pitfalls.name: Dependency drift
pitfalls.failure: Generated artifacts or runtime behavior change without a pinned toolchain and cohort.

pitfalls.name: Unreproducible state
pitfalls.failure: A claim cannot be rebuilt from content-addressed source, configuration, and durable events.

pitfalls.name: Documentation drift
pitfalls.failure: Dated prose is read as current implementation truth after code and default paths changed.

pitfalls.name: Repeated rediscovery
pitfalls.failure: Agents repeatedly relearn decisions, boundaries, and failures because they are not source-addressed and queryable.

pitfalls.name: Beautiful visualization lie
pitfalls.failure: A polished graph hides stale, missing, inferred, or disputed data behind one authoritative-looking surface.

pitfalls.name: Atlas omission
pitfalls.failure: Files, symbols, tests, events, or uncertainty disappear because a parser or visualization cannot represent them.
